title: Continuous telemetry enables linkage of multiple observations to the same wearer
description: Heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps collected continuously by the wearable can be correlated over time to link many records and sessions to the same individual wearer, even if explicit identifiers are absent.
assumptions: The device or associated system stores or transmits telemetry with persistent device identifiers, stable pseudonyms, or sufficiently distinctive patterns over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability may vary by catalog version.

title: Sensor telemetry can identify the wearer
description: Location traces, activity patterns, and physiological telemetry may uniquely identify the wearer directly or indirectly, especially when combined with timestamps or other available context.
assumptions: Telemetry is accessible to the device platform, backend, apps, or attackers with auxiliary information for re-identification.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact identifiability node may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Collection reveals sensitive information about health, habits, and whereabouts
description: Continuous capture of heart rate, steps, GPS position, and timestamps can disclose sensitive personal information such as health status, daily routines, exercise habits, home/work locations, and presence at sensitive places.
assumptions: The wearable or connected ecosystem can access raw or derived telemetry and infer higher-level attributes from it.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; disclosure subtree numbering may vary.

title: Data collection may exceed what is necessary for core functionality
description: Continuous collection of fine-grained GPS and physiological telemetry may be more detailed or more frequent than necessary for the stated purpose, creating a data minimization risk.
assumptions: Not all captured fields or sampling rates are strictly required for the immediate wearable functionality requested by the user.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for data minimization/excessive collection; exact node id may differ.

title: Wearer may be insufficiently aware of ongoing continuous sensing
description: The wearer may not fully understand that the device continuously captures multiple telemetry types, the granularity of GPS/timestamps, or the downstream uses and retention of this data.
assumptions: Notices, onboarding, or just-in-time indicators are absent, unclear, or not salient during continuous operation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for unawareness; exact node id may vary.

title: Continuous telemetry collection may occur without valid or sufficiently specific consent
description: Capturing health-related and location telemetry continuously may require explicit, informed, and granular consent; if consent is bundled, implied, or not refreshed when purposes change, non-compliance risks arise.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy requires a lawful basis, transparency, purpose limitation, and possibly explicit consent for health/location data processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for consent/lawfulness non-compliance; exact node id may differ by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Stable device identifier enables linking of activity batches over time
description: The wearable sends a persistent device id together with exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps. This allows records from multiple syncs to be linked to the same person or device over time, enabling longitudinal profiling of behavior and routines.
assumptions: The device id is stable across sync sessions and visible to the companion app or its downstream storage.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via persistent identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: GPS traces and timestamps allow linking with external datasets
description: Fine-grained location traces and timestamps received by the companion app can be correlated with external information such as home/work addresses, public event attendance, or other app data, linking the synced data to a specific individual.
assumptions: The app stores or processes sufficiently precise GPS and time data, and external auxiliary data is available.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability through quasi-identifiers and contextual data.

title: Exercise and location data can identify the user
description: Exercise sessions combined with GPS traces, timestamps, and device id can directly or indirectly identify the user by revealing habitual routes, home/work locations, and unique movement patterns.
assumptions: The companion app has access to raw or only lightly transformed sync data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from direct and indirect identifiers; exact node id may differ.

title: Sync data reveals sensitive habits and activities
description: The synced sensor batches expose personal exercise behavior, daily routines, frequented places, and potentially health-related inferences. The companion app can derive sensitive information such as fitness level, sleep/wake patterns, or visits to sensitive locations.
assumptions: The app retains enough detail from sessions and GPS traces to support behavioral inference.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of personal information through received content and inference.

title: Unprotected transmission may disclose raw sensor batches in transit
description: If the sync channel between wearable and companion app lacks strong transport protection or secure pairing, nearby attackers or malware on the phone could intercept exercise sessions, GPS traces, device id, and timestamps during synchronization.
assumptions: Transport security, authenticated pairing, or local channel protections may be weak or misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure during communication; exact node id may vary depending on the threat tree version.

title: Users may be unaware that sync data enables secondary inferences
description: A user may understand that workout data is synced, but not realize that combining GPS traces, timestamps, and device identifiers allows inference of home/work locations, routines, social relationships, or sensitive visits.
assumptions: The app's notices or UI do not clearly explain the scope of inferences enabled by the synced data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of user awareness/transparency; exact node id may differ.

title: Collection of precise GPS traces may exceed necessity for core sync purpose
description: For many companion-app functions, syncing full-resolution GPS traces and stable device identifiers may be more data than necessary. Excessive collection or retention would create a non-compliance risk with data minimization and purpose limitation principles.
assumptions: The app could fulfill core functionality with reduced precision, aggregation, or shorter retention.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance with minimization/purpose limitation; exact node id may vary.

title: Lack of verifiable sync records can impede dispute resolution
description: If the companion app does not maintain trustworthy records of what data was synced and when, the user may be unable to prove or dispute whether particular exercise sessions or location traces were transferred, affecting accountability and privacy rights handling.
assumptions: There is no reliable audit trail or user-visible sync history.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation/accountability gaps; applicability depends on whether disputeability is in scope for this flow.

title: Continuous syncing enables broad detectability of user activity patterns
description: Even without inspecting full content, the presence, timing, and frequency of sync events from the wearable to the app can reveal when the user is active, exercising, traveling, or wearing the device, making private behavior detectable.
assumptions: An observer on the phone, local network, or nearby radio channel can observe sync occurrence metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability from communication metadata; exact node id may differ.

title: Meal, calorie, and weight entries can be linked to the identified user account/device
description: The companion app may associate manually entered meals, calorie intake, and weight records with the wearer's account, device identifiers, or persistent app identifiers, enabling linkage of sensitive health and lifestyle data to the same individual over time.
assumptions: The app maintains a persistent user account, device binding, or stable identifier for storing entries.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via persistent identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Dietary and weight logs may be linked across time to build detailed behavior profiles
description: Repeated manual logging of meals, calories, and weight enables the app to correlate entries across days and weeks, revealing routines, dieting behavior, health trends, and potentially special-category inferences such as medical conditions or pregnancy.
assumptions: Historical entries are retained and queryable together within the app or backend.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for cross-context/time linkability; exact numbering may differ.

title: Meal and weight entries disclose sensitive health and lifestyle information to the app
description: The user provides highly sensitive personal data, including food habits, calorie intake, and body weight. These data can directly disclose health status, dieting practices, religion or culture-related food choices, or other intimate lifestyle attributes to the app operator.
assumptions: The app or its operator can access raw user-entered values.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for direct disclosure of content to an unintended or overly broad recipient.

title: Derived inferences from logs may disclose additional sensitive attributes
description: Even if individual entries seem benign, the app can infer sensitive facts such as eating disorders, chronic disease management, pregnancy, religious observance, or other health-related conditions from patterns in calorie, meal, and weight logs.
assumptions: The app performs analytics or personnel can inspect trends over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for inference-based detectability/disclosure; exact node id may differ.

title: User may be unable to deny or contest submitted nutrition and weight entries
description: If the app stores manual entries without clear provenance, edit history, or confirmation records, the wearer may later be unable to prove that an entry was mistyped, auto-filled, altered, or submitted by someone else using the device.
assumptions: Entries are stored as authoritative records and may influence recommendations or reports.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of repudiation handling around user-submitted data; exact numbering may vary.

title: Users may be unaware of how nutrition and weight logs are used or shared
description: The wearer may not understand whether manually entered meals, calories, and weight are used only for local tracking or also for profiling, recommendations, research, advertising, or sharing with third parties, undermining informed expectations.
assumptions: The app's notices or UI do not fully explain downstream uses at the point of collection.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for insufficient transparency/unawareness at collection.

title: Collection of detailed meal and weight data may exceed necessity or valid consent
description: Capturing granular dietary intake and weight information may be unnecessary for some app functions, or may require explicit consent and special handling because the data can reveal health information. Collecting or processing it without an appropriate legal basis, purpose limitation, or data minimization could violate privacy requirements.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy treats these data as sensitive or health-related, and the app collects them beyond strictly necessary functionality.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance relating to lawful basis, minimization, and sensitive-data handling; exact node id may differ.

title: Observation of manual entry by nearby parties can disclose sensitive information
description: Because the wearer manually types meals, calories, and weight into the app, people nearby may observe the screen or input process, learning sensitive dietary or body-weight information.
assumptions: The app is used in public or shared environments without screen privacy protections.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible disclosure threat on the user-to-app flow, but the exact LINDDUN Pro node id for shoulder-surfing/observable input may differ.

title: Sensitive health logs can be disclosed from the health log store
description: The health log store contains detailed calorie intake, weight history, and exercise-session records. If access controls, encryption, or isolation are insufficient, unauthorized parties may read these records and learn sensitive health and lifestyle information about the user.
assumptions: The datastore persists logs beyond transient processing and may be accessible by backend components, administrators, or attackers if not properly protected.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for stored-data disclosure; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Health log records may enable identification of the user
description: Even if direct identifiers are minimized, longitudinal weight, calorie, and exercise patterns in the store can be linked to a specific individual, especially when combined with account, device, or timing metadata.
assumptions: Stored records are associated with an account, device, or other metadata that could support re-identification.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability from stored personal data.

title: Longitudinal health logs can link multiple activities to the same user
description: The datastore aggregates repeated entries over time, allowing separate meals, weigh-ins, and exercise sessions to be linked into a detailed profile of one person's habits and health trajectory.
assumptions: Records are stored under a stable account, pseudonym, device identifier, or other persistent key.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via persistent records in a datastore.

title: Stored health logs may reveal highly detectable sensitive attributes
description: The presence and content of calorie intake, weight history, and exercise logs make it easy to detect that a person is using a health-tracking function and may reveal sensitive attributes such as dieting behavior, weight changes, or fitness routines.
assumptions: An observer can access the existence of records, metadata, or contents in the datastore.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability of sensitive activity/data presence; exact subtree may differ.

title: Users may be unaware of the extent and persistence of health-log storage
description: The app-to-store write flow may persist detailed health logs without users fully understanding what categories are stored, how long they are retained, or who can access them, undermining transparency and informed expectations.
assumptions: Not all storage, retention, and sharing details are clearly communicated in the app UX or privacy notices.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency around data storage.

title: Health-log storage may exceed consent or purpose limitations
description: Writing calorie, weight, and exercise data to the health log store may be non-compliant if the storage is broader than necessary, retained too long, reused for secondary purposes, or performed without valid explicit consent where required for health-related data.
assumptions: Health logs are regulated or treated as sensitive personal data, and compliance obligations apply to collection, storage, retention, and secondary use.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance relating to consent, purpose limitation, or data minimization.

title: The app may be unable to prove what health data was written and when
description: If the mobile app does not create reliable audit records for writes to the health log store, disputes may arise about whether a user entered certain calorie, weight, or exercise records, or whether the app stored them correctly.
assumptions: There is a need to resolve disputes about data entry, synchronization, or record provenance.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central for this privacy flow; node id is a best estimate for lack of evidence/provenance of data submission.

title: Stored location traces enable linkage of records to the same individual over time
description: GPS traces with timestamps written to the location history store can be linked together to build a persistent mobility profile for one user or device across days, places, and sessions. Even if direct identifiers are absent, repeated trajectories are highly linkable.
assumptions: The store retains multiple traces per user/device or otherwise preserves a stable key, account reference, or consistent pseudonym.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether linkage is modeled at data-store contents or identifiers.

title: Location history can identify an individual through unique mobility patterns
description: Fine-grained GPS coordinates with timestamps are often uniquely identifying. Home/work inference and repeated route patterns can reveal the identity of the person behind the stored traces, even without explicit names in the dataset.
assumptions: Stored traces are sufficiently precise and retained long enough to infer habitual locations or correlate with external knowledge.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability from quasi-identifiers/inferred identity.

title: Location history discloses sensitive habits, places, and routines
description: The stored GPS traces and timestamps reveal visits to sensitive locations and behavioral patterns, such as home address, workplace, religious venues, clinics, political events, and daily routines. This exceeds what may be necessary for many app functions.
assumptions: The store contains raw or high-resolution traces rather than heavily aggregated summaries.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node; exact subtree may differ depending on whether disclosure is direct from raw data or via inference.

title: Inference from historical traces reveals additional private attributes
description: Even if the app only stores coordinates and timestamps, analysis of the history can infer private attributes such as home/work locations, social relationships, health status, religion, or lifestyle. These inferred attributes constitute additional privacy disclosure risk.
assumptions: Historical data is available for analysis and can be combined with maps or external datasets.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to capture inference-based disclosure from stored data.

title: Users may be unaware that detailed location history is being persistently stored
description: Writing GPS traces with timestamps into a location history store may be insufficiently visible to users. If collection and retention are not transparent, users may not understand that continuous historical tracking is occurring.
assumptions: The app UX does not clearly signal ongoing storage, retention period, or downstream uses of location history.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node; exact subtree depends on whether notice, consent, or retention transparency is emphasized.

title: Collection and retention of detailed location history may be non-compliant with data minimization or purpose limitation
description: Persistently storing raw GPS traces with timestamps can exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose, especially if retained indefinitely or reused for analytics beyond the original function. This creates risk of non-compliance with privacy obligations around minimization, retention limits, and lawful basis.
assumptions: The system stores detailed traces longer than necessary, or uses them for secondary purposes without an appropriate legal basis or user choice.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact LINDDUN Pro node depends on the compliance obligation being modeled.

title: App may be unable to prove or contest what location data was written
description: If the mobile app does not create trustworthy records of when and what location traces were stored, disputes may arise about whether certain locations were recorded, altered, or submitted by the user/device. This can undermine accountability around sensitive location processing.
assumptions: There is no tamper-evident audit trail or integrity protection for write events to the location history store.
uncertainty_note: Applicability is lower than other threats for this flow; node id is an approximate fit for repudiation/accountability of data submission.

title: Cross-session health logs enable linkage of records to the same individual
description: The analytics service reads calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions from the health log store. Even if individual entries were collected at different times, stable identifiers, account references, device identifiers, or consistent behavioral patterns can allow records to be linked together and tied to one person over time.
assumptions: The store or query context contains a persistent identifier, account key, or sufficiently distinctive quasi-identifiers to correlate entries across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers/correlation across sessions.

title: Health-condition analysis may identify the data subject from sensitive log patterns
description: Calorie, weight, and exercise histories are highly distinctive and sensitive. When the analytics service processes these logs for health-condition analysis, the combination of longitudinal measurements may directly identify or single out a person, especially when combined with account context or other available attributes.
assumptions: The analytics service has access to user/account context or the data itself is sufficiently unique to single out individuals.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for identifiability/singling out from analyzed health data.

title: Health-condition inference discloses sensitive information beyond the original logs
description: By reading calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions, the analytics service can infer sensitive health conditions, lifestyle traits, or risk factors that were not explicitly provided in a single record. This creates a disclosure threat because derived insights may reveal more than the user expects from the raw logs alone.
assumptions: The service derives or exposes analytical outputs, scores, or classifications based on the stored logs.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best estimate for inference/disclosure of sensitive derived information.

title: Secondary analytics use may be unexpected to the user
description: Users may provide calorie, weight, and exercise logs for tracking purposes, but not expect longitudinal health-condition analysis across sessions. If this purpose is not transparent, the processing can be unawareness: individuals may not understand that their historical logs are being mined to derive health-related conclusions.
assumptions: The system does not clearly communicate this analytical purpose at collection time or before processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for lack of user awareness about secondary/derived analytics use.

title: Health analytics processing may exceed consent or stated purpose
description: Reading historical calorie, weight, and exercise logs for health-condition analysis may be incompatible with the original purpose for which the logs were collected, or may require explicit consent due to the sensitivity of health-related inferences. If the analytics service performs this processing without an adequate legal basis or outside declared retention/use limits, it creates non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Applicable policy, consent terms, or regulation restrict secondary use of health-related data or inferred health status.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best estimate for non-compliance due to purpose limitation/consent issues.

title: Cross-session location history enables linkage of records to the same individual
description: The analytics query uses location history across sessions, allowing records from multiple sessions to be linked together into a persistent mobility profile for the same person. Even if session identifiers were originally separate, the datastore supports correlation over time.
assumptions: Location history entries contain stable identifiers, account references, device identifiers, or sufficiently unique spatiotemporal patterns to associate sessions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability via correlating records across sessions; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Daily routine inference can identify the individual behind pseudonymous data
description: Deriving daily routine and movement patterns from historical locations can reveal home, workplace, and habitual visits. These patterns may allow the analytics service or downstream recipients to identify a person even if direct identifiers are absent.
assumptions: Routine locations such as home/work are sufficiently distinctive and may be combined with auxiliary knowledge.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identifiability through inference from quasi-identifying location patterns.

title: Movement-pattern analytics disclose sensitive habits and behaviors
description: Querying and analyzing location history across sessions can disclose private information such as religious attendance, medical visits, political participation, intimate relationships, or other sensitive habits inferred from repeated visits and trajectories.
assumptions: The stored location history has enough granularity and retention to infer sensitive places or recurring behaviors.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure by inference from stored location traces; exact numbering may differ.

title: Secondary use of location history for behavioral profiling may exceed user expectations
description: Using historical location data to derive daily routines and movement patterns may go beyond the purpose users understood when the data was collected, reducing predictability and intervenability over how their location history is used.
assumptions: Users were not clearly informed that cross-session analytics and profiling would be performed for this purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id under unawareness/unexpected processing; exact LINDDUN Pro node numbering may vary.

title: Cross-session routine analysis may violate purpose limitation or data minimization
description: The analytics service processes extensive historical location data to derive movement patterns, which may be more data than necessary for the original service purpose or incompatible with the purpose for which the location data was collected.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements impose purpose limitation, proportionality, retention limits, or data minimization on location data processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance with purpose limitation/data minimization; exact numbering may differ.

title: Sensitive health inferences disclosed in transit to the mobile app
description: The analytics service sends inferred health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags to the companion app. If the flow is exposed to unauthorized parties during transmission or via insecure API responses, highly sensitive inferred health information could be disclosed.
assumptions: The flow traverses a network or IPC boundary where interception, logging, or unauthorized access is possible.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a generic information disclosure of message contents; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary by catalog wording.

title: Exposure of inferred insights through app-side notifications, caches, or local display
description: Once received by the mobile app, inferred insights such as risk indicators or trend flags may be exposed through lock-screen notifications, screenshots, local caches, debug logs, or display to someone other than the intended user.
assumptions: The app stores, renders, or notifies on the returned insights and the device may be shared, unlocked, or observable by others.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-effort for disclosure at the receiving endpoint rather than in transit.

title: Inference reveals new sensitive personal information beyond raw input data
description: The analytics service derives health-condition risk indicators and trend flags that may reveal sensitive attributes or likely future conditions that the user did not explicitly provide. Returning these inferences to the app increases the amount and sensitivity of personal data processed and exposed.
assumptions: The inferred insights are not merely restatements of user-provided data but constitute newly derived sensitive information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/disclosure-related node for derived sensitive information; exact LINDDUN Pro placement of inference threats may differ.

title: Users may not understand the meaning or confidence of inferred health insights
description: Risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags may be presented without sufficient explanation of how they were derived, their confidence, limitations, or appropriate interpretation. This can undermine user awareness and informed decision-making about the processing and use of their data.
assumptions: The app presents concise analytics outputs and may omit provenance, confidence scores, or explanatory context.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort mapping to lack of user awareness/transparency.

title: Processing and sharing inferred health data may exceed consent or stated purpose
description: Returning inferred health-condition risks and behavioral summaries to the app may go beyond the purpose originally understood by the user, especially if the user consented to tracking or wellness features but not to generation of sensitive health inferences.
assumptions: Consent, notice, or legal basis may not explicitly cover creation and delivery of inferred health insights.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort non-compliance mapping; exact node depends on the applicable legal basis, consent, and purpose-limitation structure.

title: Returned analytics can link multiple observations into a persistent health profile
description: The set of routine summaries, trend flags, and risk indicators sent from the analytics service can enable the app or anyone with access to it to link multiple periods of behavior and health observations into a persistent, longitudinal profile of the user.
assumptions: Insights are associated with a stable account, device, or user identifier over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to linkability created by repeated analytics outputs.

title: Exposure of inferred health-risk indicators on the app screen to bystanders
description: The dashboard presents sensitive inferred condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals). When displayed on the mobile screen, nearby people, shoulder surfers, or anyone viewing notifications/screenshots may learn private health-related information about the user without authorization.
assumptions: The app displays these indicators in clear text/graphics on-screen and may be opened in environments where others can observe the display.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for disclosure of data in presentation/display context; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: Strong identifiability of the user through personalized health inferences
description: The displayed trends and inferred condition indicators are highly individualized and health-related. Anyone who can view the dashboard can directly associate these sensitive inferences with the specific wearer using the device, increasing identifiability of the user's health status.
assumptions: The app session is tied to a known individual and the device is used personally by that wearer.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability; exact subnode may differ depending on the threat-tree variant used.

title: Linkability of multiple sensitive observations across time via dashboard trends
description: Displaying longitudinal trends allows viewers with repeated access to link multiple observations over time to the same wearer, revealing patterns in behavior and health-risk evolution that may not be apparent from a single data point.
assumptions: The dashboard exposes historical trend views or repeated snapshots can be observed.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability across observations; exact subnode may vary.

title: Insufficient user awareness that the app is inferring sensitive conditions
description: The user may not understand how the app derives eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals, what data sources are used, how reliable the inference is, or the consequences of viewing/sharing these indicators. This undermines informed understanding of the privacy impact of the displayed output.
assumptions: The dashboard does not fully explain inference logic, confidence, provenance, or privacy implications.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unawareness; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Potential non-compliance in presenting inferred health data without adequate safeguards or transparency
description: Displaying inferred health-risk indicators to the user may trigger legal or policy obligations around transparency, accuracy disclaimers, special-category health data handling, and user rights. If the app presents these inferences without appropriate notices, controls, or justification, the flow may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Applicable law/policy treats inferred condition indicators as sensitive health-related personal data and imposes transparency and protection requirements.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit placeholder for non-compliance; exact subnode depends on the compliance obligations in scope.

title: Third-party cloud provider can inspect hosted health and location data
description: The full health and location dataset, analytics data, and models are hosted at an external cloud provider. Provider personnel or provider-side services may be able to access plaintext data, revealing sensitive health conditions, movements, and inferred attributes about individuals.
assumptions: Data is stored or replicated in a form accessible to the cloud provider or its administrators; encryption or confidential computing protections are absent, weak, or provider-controlled.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a best-fit disclosure-from-storage/access threat; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary by catalog version.

title: Cloud-hosted full dataset enables linkage across health and location domains
description: Combining complete health records with location history in one hosted environment enables the cloud provider or anyone gaining access there to link records across domains and build rich profiles of the same individuals.
assumptions: Common identifiers, quasi-identifiers, account metadata, or stable device/location patterns exist that allow records to be correlated.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability due to cross-dataset correlation; exact node id may differ in some LINDDUN Pro trees.

title: Individuals can be identified from hosted health and location dataset
description: Even if direct identifiers are minimized, the combination of detailed health data and location traces at the cloud provider can permit re-identification of individuals through unique patterns, rare conditions, or movement histories.
assumptions: Dataset contains sufficiently granular timestamps, locations, health events, or other quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit identifiability node; exact node id may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Third-party hosting and replication may exceed consent or lawful processing expectations
description: Hosting and replicating the full health and location dataset with an external cloud provider may be incompatible with the purposes, consent scope, contractual commitments, or legal basis under which the data was originally collected.
assumptions: Data subjects were not clearly informed about third-party hosting/replication, cross-border storage, or secondary processing by the provider.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node for unlawful or out-of-scope third-party processing; exact node id may differ.

title: Opaque third-party replication reduces user awareness of where sensitive data resides
description: Users may not understand that their full health and location dataset, analytics outputs, and models are replicated to and stored by a cloud provider, making processing locations, retention, and access paths insufficiently transparent.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-product explanations do not clearly disclose third-party hosting, replication, and related implications.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness/transparency node; exact node id may vary.

title: Cloud replication and backups hinder deletion of sensitive data
description: Replication of the full dataset across cloud storage tiers, regions, snapshots, and backups can make complete erasure difficult, causing health and location data to persist longer than intended or after deletion requests.
assumptions: Provider uses redundant storage, backups, or disaster-recovery replicas that are not promptly purged.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/deletion-related node in LINDDUN Pro; exact node id may differ by catalog version.
